title: Proper direct image preserves direct sums
statement:
Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. For $p$ proper, $Rp_*\colon\Dic(X,\Lambda)\to\Dic(Y,\Lambda)$
([sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window]) preserves arbitrary direct sums.

proof.text: Fix a small family $(K_\alpha)$ in $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ and write $S=\bigoplus_\alpha K_\alpha$. By [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums], $S$ lies in $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ and these sums are the ambient derived sums. Let $c:\bigoplus_\alpha Rp_*K_\alpha\to Rp_*S$ be the canonical comparison: if $i_\alpha:K_\alpha\to S$ and $j_\alpha:Rp_*K_\alpha\to\bigoplus_\beta Rp_*K_\beta$ are the coprojections, then $c j_\alpha=Rp_*(i_\alpha)$. We will prove that this particular map is an isomorphism locally on $Y$. No integer bounding the fibres of $p$ globally is chosen.

source.place: Paragraph 2: the arbitrary family and its canonical comparison.

proof.text: Let $a:U\hookrightarrow Y$ be an affine open and put $X_U=X\times_YU$, $b:X_U\hookrightarrow X$, and $p_U:X_U\to U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], $p_U$ is proper, hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The affine $U$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] to obtain an integer $d_U\geq0$ such that every ordinary fibre $(X_U)_y$, $y\in U$, has topological Krull dimension at most $d_U$. The definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] supplies affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}C$ over affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $U$ with $C$ a finitely generated $A$-algebra; tensoring a finite generating set with $\kappa(y)$ shows that the fibre charts $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, $B_i=C_i\otimes_A\kappa(y)$, are finite type over $\kappa(y)$, and they form an open cover of $(X_U)_y$. All dimensions below are topological Krull dimensions. An open subspace has dimension at most that of the ambient space, and a space covered by opens has dimension the supremum of theirs (Stacks 0B7I, `topology.tex`, `lemma-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions`, and the remark before it); both are elementary from the chain definition. Hence $\dim\operatorname{Spec}B_i\leq d_U$. The geometric fibre $(X_U)_{\bar y}=(X_U)_y\times_{\kappa(y)}\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(y)}$ is covered by the opens $\operatorname{Spec}(\overline{\kappa(y)}\otimes_{\kappa(y)}B_i)$, whose dimensions equal $\dim\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-preserved-field-extension]; so $\dim(X_U)_{\bar y}\leq d_U$. An empty fibre stays empty. The integer may vary with $U$.

source.place: Local repair of paragraph 2, before choosing its finite window: use Stacks 0A3V and 00P3 on each affine base open.

proof.text: For either open immersion $h=a,b$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies its pro-etale site with the corresponding localized site. The ringed restriction comparison [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-comparison] and [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identify $h^*$ with ordinary restriction with the actual ring $\Lambda$ pulled back from the point; it is exact. Here $E$ is a finite subextension of the fixed $\Qlb/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $\Qlb$ has the condensed finite-subextension convention specified in that theorem. We use only its untwisted assertion, which imposes no invertibility hypothesis on $\ell$. Thus $H^n(h^*L)=h^*H^n(L)$. The adjunction $h^*\dashv h_*$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] shows that $h^*$ preserves colimits: maps from $h^*(\operatorname{colim}M_i)$ to $N$ are compatible families of maps $M_i\to h_*N$, equivalently compatible families of maps $h^*M_i\to N$. By [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], the derived adjunction is $Lh^*\dashv Rh_*$. The exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] identifies $Lh^*$ with termwise restriction; the same Hom calculation gives $h^*(\bigoplus L_i)\simeq\bigoplus h^*L_i$ in the unbounded derived categories, with the coprojections preserved. For open restriction $h:W\hookrightarrow Z$ ($h=b$) and $C$ constructible on $Z$ by [sk-def-sfb-constructible], we show $h^*C$ is constructible on $W$. First, on a qcqs scheme the global condition (a finite stratification by constructible locally closed subschemes on whose strata the module has a finite constant local model) and the affine-local condition agree. Global implies local: for an affine open $V$, $V\to Z$ is quasi-compact, so the traces $Z_a\cap V$ are constructible locally closed in $V$, they stratify $V$ via $Z_a\times_ZV\to V$, and a local model on $\{U_i\to Z_a\}$ pulls back along $U_i\times_ZV$ because $\Lambda_{U_i}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_i$ restricts to $\Lambda_{U_i\times_ZV}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_i$. Local implies global: choose a finite affine cover $V_1,\dots,V_m$; the sets $V_k\setminus(V_1\cup\dots\cup V_{k-1})$ are constructible locally closed (quasi-compact opens of a qcqs scheme are retrocompact), and intersecting them with the strata of $V_k$ gives a finite stratification of the required kind, again by restricting local models. Thus in all cases the condition can be tested on affine opens. Now every affine open $V$ of $W$ is an affine open of $Z$, and $(h^*C)|_V=C|_V$ because the restriction identifications compose by evaluation on the localized sites; so $h^*C$ satisfies the affine-local condition, without requiring $h$ to be quasi-compact. Since $X_U$ is qcqs (proper over the affine $U$), the equivalence just proved makes $h^*C$ constructible in the global sense on $X_U$ as well. Restricting a filtered presentation of $H^n(K_\alpha)$ therefore proves $b^*K_\alpha\in\Dic(X_U,\Lambda)$.

source.place: Local restriction of paragraph 2, preserving coefficients, sums, and the input class; Stacks 00XZ and the displayed module adjunctions.

proof.text: There is a natural isomorphism $\theta_L:a^*Rp_*L\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{U,*}b^*L$ for every unbounded $L$. Indeed, the definition [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] gives $(p_*M)(T)=M(T\times_YX)$ on underlying abelian sheaves; [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] gives this same pushforward with its induced module action. If $T\to U$ is pro-etale, $T\times_YX=T\times_UX_U$, so $a^*p_*M=p_{U,*}b^*M$, including the actions, naturally in $M$: a coefficient section on $T$ acts on $M(T\times_YX)$ through its pullback to $T\times_YX$, and under $T\times_YX=T\times_UX_U$ this is the identical coefficient section and action on $M(T\times_UX_U)$. Choose a K-injective resolution $L\to I$. By [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], $b^*$ is right adjoint to the exact module functor $b_!$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] makes $b^*I$ K-injective. By [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], $p_*I$ and $p_{U,*}b^*I$ compute the two derived images. The preceding equality of complexes and exactness of restriction yield $\theta_L$. Naturality holds because the equality is natural on complexes and hence on their localization.

source.place: Local restriction of paragraph 2: K-injective computation of the canonical open restriction comparison; Stacks 08BJ and 08FI.

proof.text: Apply [det-proper-unbounded-window-ii-general] with its schemes $X,Y$ replaced by $X_U,U$, its proper morphism by $p_U$, its geometric-fibre bound $d$ by the nonnegative integer $d_U$ from step 2, and its family by $(b^*K_\alpha)$, whose terms lie in $\Dic(X_U,\Lambda)$ by step 3. Its coefficients remain the same $E$ or $\Qlb$. Its conclusion is invertibility of the canonical comparison $c_U:\bigoplus_\alpha Rp_{U,*}b^*K_\alpha\to Rp_{U,*}(\bigoplus_\alpha b^*K_\alpha)$. Thus it applies with exactly its stated global-bound hypothesis on this restricted morphism. The existing detail node carries the bounded-family induction and finite-window argument; this step uses only its statement.

source.place: Paragraph 2, existing general detail node, now applied on the affine open $U$.

proof.text: Under the coproduct identifications of step 3 and $\theta$ of step 4, $a^*c$ is exactly $c_U$. To check the map, identify $b^*S$ with $\bigoplus_\alpha b^*K_\alpha$. On the $\alpha$th coprojection the transported $a^*c$ is $\theta_S\,a^*(Rp_*i_\alpha)\,\theta_{K_\alpha}^{-1}=Rp_{U,*}(b^*i_\alpha)$ by naturality of $\theta$. These are precisely the defining components of $c_U$, so the coproduct universal property gives equality. Thus $a^*c$ is an isomorphism for every affine open $U\subseteq Y$.

source.place: Paragraph 2: compatibility of the canonical comparison with restriction; explicit coprojection calculation.

proof.text: For each integer $n$, exactness of restriction gives $a^*H^n(c)=H^n(a^*c)$, an isomorphism on every affine open. Hence the kernel and cokernel of $H^n(c)$ restrict to zero on an affine cover. A module sheaf zero on this cover is zero: for any pro-etale $T\to Y$, the opens $T\times_YU$ cover $T$, and every section vanishes on them, so vanishes by the separatedness axiom of a sheaf. Thus both kernel and cokernel are zero, and $H^n(c)$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] for all $n$ to conclude that $c$ is an isomorphism in the ambient unbounded derived category.

source.place: Paragraph 2, final cohomological isomorphism test, with Zariski locality written out (Stacks 05RT).

proof.text: Finally, the functor $Rp_*:\Dic(X,\Lambda)\to\Dic(Y,\Lambda)$ of the statement is the one the statement cites, [sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window]: that node supplies it, i.e. proves $Rp_*(\Dic(X,\Lambda))\subseteq\Dic(Y,\Lambda)$, for $p$ proper together with an integer $d$ bounding the dimensions of all geometric fibres of $p$ (the setting of the source, where $p$ and $d$ are those of the heart-bound lemma that the cited node names). In that setting it gives $Rp_*K_\alpha\in\Dic(Y,\Lambda)$ for every $\alpha$ and $Rp_*S\in\Dic(Y,\Lambda)$, using $S\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ from step 1. The category $\Dic(Y,\Lambda)$ is by definition the full subcategory of the ambient derived category on objects whose cohomology is ind-constructible, with ambient morphisms. By [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums] it is closed under ambient coproducts, which are therefore its coproducts: the same morphisms and the ambient coprojection universal property give the universal property in this full subcategory. Consequently $c$, which is the canonical comparison in $\Dic(Y,\Lambda)$, and its ambient inverse from step 7 are morphisms of $\Dic(Y,\Lambda)$, and the two inverse equations still hold. The canonical coproduct comparison is invertible there for every small family, as asserted. Steps 1--7 do not use $d$: for an arbitrary proper $p$, e.g. $\coprod_n\mathbf P^n_k\to\coprod_n\operatorname{Spec}k$ with unbounded fibre dimensions, they still give invertibility of the ambient comparison $c$; only the membership of its source and target in $\Dic(Y,\Lambda)$ is taken from [sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window].

source.place: Statement of sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window: '$Rp_*$ ... maps $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ into $\Dic(Y,\Lambda)$', with $p,d$ as in sk-lem-proper-heart-bound; conclusion of the unit statement.

split_report.summary: Eight-step split, no new nodes. Steps 1-7 prove invertibility of the canonical ambient comparison for every proper p, by restriction to affine opens U of Y, a local geometric-fibre bound d_U, the existing det-proper-unbounded-window-ii-general on p_U, and Zariski descent of the isomorphism. Step 8 identifies it with the coproduct comparison in Dic(Y), taking membership of Rp_*K_alpha and Rp_*S in Dic(Y) from sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window, the functor the statement cites (proved there under a global geometric-fibre bound d, the source's setting). Landing-refusal repair: step 3 updated to the current cartesian-coefficient and derived-category statements; the hypothesis-restricted triangulated-subcategory citation removed. Maintainer reader (2026-10-17): step 8 now cites the window lemma for membership; step 3 writes out agreement of the global and affine-local constructibility conditions on qcqs schemes; step 2 uses topological dimensions throughout (Stacks 0B7I) instead of the local-ring dimension of lem-pc-dimension-affine-open-cover, which is no longer cited. The imported statement is unchanged; no statement correction is made.
split_report.blueprint: Unit paragraph 1 is realized by det-proper-unbounded-window-ii-bounded through det-proper-unbounded-window-ii-general. Paragraph 2 is applied on each affine open of Y in steps 2-5 via det-proper-unbounded-window-ii-general; steps 6-7 descend the canonical comparison. Step 8 gives the displayed restricted-functor conclusion using the corestriction of sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window cited in the statement.

tool_uses.why: Ambient sums and cohomology, and Dic closure under sums; no proper-image argument is replaced.
Local finite fibre dimension bound on a quasi-compact base; the unit does not supply its geometric dimension argument.
Replace ordinary fibres by geometric fibres without changing the chart dimensions.
Identify open pro-etale restriction with localization, without using a proper base-change theorem.
Identify the actual ringed module pullback with slice restriction for the pulled-back condensed coefficients.
The coefficient comparison is invertible and module pullback is exact for E and Qlb.
Exact open extension by zero makes its right adjoint preserve K-injective resolutions.

split_report.proof_correction: The unit's second paragraph uses a global d, which is available in its setting (p and d as in sk-lem-proper-heart-bound, inherited through the statement's citation of sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window) but not from properness alone: coprod_n P^n_k -> coprod_n Spec k is proper with unbounded fibre dimensions. Steps 2-7 prove the ambient comparison using affine-local bounds d_U for arbitrary proper p, which is what the citer det-proper-image-localizing-proper uses. Membership in Dic(Y) of source and target of the comparison (step 8) is taken from sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window and therefore needs its global bound; whether Rp_* preserves Dic without such a bound is not asserted or proved here. No statement correction is made.
split_report.source_error: The existing bounded detail proof has H^n(C[-a])=H^{n+a}(C); the correct cohomological convention is H^n(C[-a])=H^{n-a}(C). For C concentrated in degree zero and a=1, C[-1] is in degree 1. Only the bounded detail statement is used through the existing general node. The separate source/dependency typo is reported for maintenance, not reproduced or edited here.
